extracted.intended_audience: prospective NINDS F32 applicants and their mentors (postdoctoral fellows and sponsoring investigators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and review criteria for preparing and submitting an NINDS-specific NRSA (F32) postdoctoral fellowship application, including eligibility, application content expectations, and review considerations unique to the NINDS mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility window and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are eligible to apply within approximately 12 months prior to joining a postdoctoral laboratory to within the first 12 months of starting in that laboratory (18 months for resubmissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support may be requested for a first or subsequent mentored postdoctoral position. Applicants are encouraged to apply early in their eligibility window because the NINDS F32 only supports postdoctoral fellows during the first 4 years (maximum of 36 months) in a given postdoctoral laboratory; delays in applying reduce the total months of possible support (example: receiving award 6 months into 2nd postdoc year leaves up to 30 months of support). Reviewers consider applicant exposure to the lab when evaluating sophistication; those applying earlier (<3 months) may have less sophisticated understanding but appear to have higher success rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant citizenship/status and academic background
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are open to U.S. citizens or permanent residents; research doctoral programs; members of underrepresented groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure eligibility is satisfied before applying; eligibility rules govern who may be funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NINDS-specific program announcement and instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The NINDS F32 has different requirements, instructions for both candidates and mentors, and review criteria than the parent NIH F32. Applicants are strongly encouraged to read the program announcement carefully and completely (Program Announcement PAR-25-234).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit under the parent NIH F32 program announcement number. Follow NINDS-specific instructions for format, content, and submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed F32 research must fall within the NINDS mission; NINDS will not accept applications that fall within the mission of other NIH institutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mission-relevance is determined by the specific aims and significance of the research according to NIH referral guidelines (not simply by the source of mentor funding). Applicants are strongly encouraged to contact the NINDS office for training and workforce development prior to applying to confirm mission relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / No project overlap with mentor's grants
rubrics_metrics.description: NINDS will not support fellowship applications if the specific aims, questions being asked or approach to answering a specific question are fundamentally identical to those already proposed in the mentor’s grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While applicants are expected to work with the mentor to develop the application, the applicant should write an original research plan consistent with the mentor’s funded research. Applicants should not simply be working towards fulfillment of specific aims already devised by the mentor. See NINDS policy on project overlap and fellowship applications for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-person singular authorship to demonstrate applicant's intellectual contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are strongly advised to write in the first person singular voice when talking about their ideas, their hypotheses, their approach, the analyses they will do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use first-person singular to make clear what the applicant is doing and what ideas/hypotheses/project components are the applicant's versus the lab's or others'. Cite other individuals where appropriate (e.g., work done by others or jointly). Writing in third person can imply someone else wrote it; explicitly distinguish what is general lab context and what will be done by the applicant so reviewers understand the applicant's intellectual contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary data are not required for the NINDS F32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data from NINDS show the percentage of applications submitted and awarded without preliminary data are similar; presence of preliminary data does not affect success rate. The lack of required preliminary data is intended to facilitate early applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers adjust expectations based on candidate exposure to lab
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are instructed to review applications in the context of how long the candidate has been exposed to the lab/project/ideas (i.e., the quality expectation should be identical, but the sophistication with regard to the project would be expected to be different).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant who submits before entering the lab is expected to have a less sophisticated understanding than someone who has been in the lab for 6 months or more; reviewers should account for this when evaluating the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration limit of support
rubrics_metrics.description: The NINDS F32 is designed to support postdoctoral fellows during the first 4 years (for a maximum of 36 months) in a given postdoctoral laboratory or research environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who apply late in their eligibility window will receive fewer months of support. Plan application timing accordingly; preliminary data are not required to enable earlier submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award transfer / change and interim arrangements require prior approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual NINDS F32 fellowship awards are made for training at a specific institution under the guidance of a particular sponsor. Prior approval by Office of Training and Workforce Development is required for a transfer of the award to another institution, a change in the primary sponsor, a significant project change, or work for more than 1 month at a different institution, unless already described in the initial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the primary sponsor plans to be absent from the institution for a continuous period of more than 3 months, an interim arrangement must be requested by the institution and approved in writing by the Office of Training and Workforce Development prior to the absence. The subsequent RPPR should describe the approved arrangement and accomplishments in light of the change of plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parental leave / extension policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows who have children while supported by this FOA, either through childbirth or adoption, are encouraged to consider requesting a six-month extension of their fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NINDS may provide one six-month extension per candidate to ensure fellowship research and training can be completed. Requests must be submitted in writing, following procedures described in the NIH Grants Policy Statement, Section 11.2.6. This is in addition to standard, automatic NIH leave policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications reviewed by NINDS Scientific Review Branch (NST4)
rubrics_metrics.description: NINDS F32 applications will be reviewed by the NINDS Scientific Review Branch (NST4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should carefully read all descriptions, instructions and review criteria in the FOA for an understanding of how the applications will be evaluated. Consult 'Applying for the NINDS F32' and related FAQs for additional details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to read FOA and contact NINDS training office
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates should carefully read all descriptions, instructions and review criteria in the FOA for an understanding of how the applications will be evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For additional FAQs see 'Applying for the NINDS F32' and contact the NINDS Fellowships contact (Jenny Kim, Ph.D.) or the Office of Training and Workforce Development as needed for clarification (e.g., mission relevance, eligibility questions).
